# Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka (Ja 454)

**ID:** Ja 454
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Ghaṭapaṇḍitajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Epigraphic and art-historical evidence from Pagan confirms that the story was well known in Burmese temple tradition under name variants such as *Ghatapandita*, *Satapandita*, and *Ghattamandita* [Win Than Tun 2002].

Scholars of comparative folklore have also compared narrative motifs found in the Jātaka to Western myths, such as the Greek story of Danae [Wick and Rabens 2013].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: Ja 352 Sujātajātaka; Ja 372 Migapotakajātaka; Ja 410 Somadattajātaka; Ja 449 Maṭṭhakuṇḍalījātaka
- Mentioned in: Pv 8 Goṇapetavatthu; Pv 18 Kaṇhapetavatthu; Pv 17 Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīpetavatthu; Pv 25 Ubbaripetavatthu; Vv 83 Maṭṭhakuṇḍalīvimānavatthu

**Sources**

- [Win Than Tun 2002] Win Than Tun, Buddhism Pagan period (2002) — Attests to the text and name variants in Pagan temple inscriptions.
- [Eliot 1921] Charles Eliot, Hinduism and Buddhism: An Historical Sketch, Vol. 2 (1921) — Discusses the Jātaka's relationship to the Krishna cycle and Brahmanical legends.
- [Thomas 1933] Edward J. Thomas, History of Buddhist Thought (1933) — Notes the presence of the Krishna story without reference to divine status.
- [Fausböll 1887] V. Fausböll, The Jātaka Together with Its Commentary, Vol. 4 (1887) — Provides the closing samodhāna, collection placement in Dasanipāta, and alternative title Ghatajātaka.
- [Wick and Rabens 2013] Peter Wick and Volker Rabens, eds., Religions and Trade (2013) — Notes comparative folklore link with the Greek myth of Danae.
